correctness.rationale: In the Ritz basis the congruence has diagonal entries θ and σ=1+(κ−1)r, r=sin²φ, and determinant κθ/ρ, ρ=κ−(κ−1)r. Its eigenvalue ratio is strictly ordered by F=(θ+σ)²ρ/(κθ). For fixed r the unique minimum is θ=σ; apply this lower bound at R=sin²Φ. At θ=σ(R), the derivative in r has the sign of 2ρ−θ−σ, positive for r<R≤1/2 because ρ(r)≥θ≥σ(r). This attains the endpoint lower bound, including the singleton Φ=0 and the derivative-zero endpoint at Φ=π/4. The endpoint matrix has equal diagonals and squared correlation z/(1+z), which gives the exact condition number, interpolating from 1 to κ. For θ=1, subtracting the unpreconditioned invariant with denominators cleared gives (κ−1)²(1−r)((κ−1)r²+3r−1), whose unique positive root yields the strict cutoff. Its angular scale is κ^(−1/4); z is comparable to κΦ² at large κ on the admitted range and tends to c² for sqrt(κ)Φ→c. These are exact-arithmetic statements in dimension two.
residual_risks: No higher-dimensional or finite-precision conclusion follows, and the result concerns spectral conditioning rather than total solver performance.
